questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the primary compositional difference between a typical comet nucleus and a typical C-type asteroid?

options.text: Comets are primarily rocky with a metallic core, while C-type asteroids are mostly icy.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not primarily rocky with a metallic core, and C-type asteroids are not mostly icy.

options.text: Comets are rich in metallic elements, while C-type asteroids are composed mainly of silicates.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not rich in metallic elements, and C-type asteroids are not composed mainly of silicates.

options.text: Comets are characterized by a significant fraction of volatile ices mixed with dust, while C-type asteroids are rich in carbonaceous silicates with little to no bulk ice.
options.explanation: This option is correct because it accurately describes the primary compositional difference between comets and C-type asteroids.

options.text: Comets are composed of solid methane and ammonia
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not composed solely of solid methane and ammonia.

questions.explanation: Comets and C-type asteroids have distinct compositions, with comets having a significant fraction of volatile ices mixed with dust, and C-type asteroids being rich in carbonaceous silicates with little to no bulk ice.

questions.question: What is the primary distinguishing characteristic between most asteroids and comets when they are near the Sun?

options.text: Asteroids are typically larger than comets.
options.explanation: Size is not the primary distinguishing characteristic between asteroids and comets.

options.text: Comets exhibit a coma and tails due to sublimation, while asteroids generally do not.
options.explanation: This is the primary distinguishing characteristic between asteroids and comets.

options.text: Asteroids have more eccentric orbits than comets.
options.explanation: Orbital eccentricity is not the primary distinguishing characteristic between asteroids and comets.

options.text: Comets are primarily composed of rock, while asteroids are primarily ice.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct composition of comets and asteroids.

questions.explanation: Comets are icy bodies that sublimate (turn directly from solid to gas) when heated by the Sun, forming a gaseous coma and dust/ion tails. Asteroids are primarily rocky bodies that do not exhibit this behavior.

questions.question: What is the primary difference in composition between the nucleus of a typical comet and a C-type (carbonaceous) asteroid?

options.text: Comets are primarily rocky, while C-type asteroids are metallic.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not primarily rocky, and C-type asteroids are not metallic.

options.text: Comets are rich in silicates and iron, while C-type asteroids are icy.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not rich in silicates and iron, and C-type asteroids are not icy.

options.text: Comets are predominantly icy with embedded dust, while C-type asteroids are rocky with organic compounds.
options.explanation: This option is correct because comets are predominantly icy with embedded dust, and C-type asteroids are rocky with organic compounds.

options.text: Comets are made of pure water ice, while C-type asteroids are made of pure carbon.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because comets are not made of pure water ice, and C-type asteroids are not made of pure carbon.

questions.explanation: Comets are often described as "dirty snowballs" or "icy dirtballs," meaning their nuclei are a mixture of water ice, frozen gases (like CO, CO2, CH4), and dust/rocky material. C-type asteroids, found mostly in the outer main belt, are primitive, undifferentiated bodies rich in carbonaceous material, silicates, and often contain hydrated minerals, but they lack significant amounts of volatiles like water ice in their bulk composition.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about comets is incorrect?

options.text: Comets are primarily composed of ice, dust, and rocky material.

options.text: The nucleus of a comet is typically a few kilometers in diameter.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: Comets develop a visible coma and tail only when they are close to the Sun.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because it is incomplete.

options.text: Comets have highly elliptical orbits that can take them far beyond Pluto.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

questions.explanation: Comets develop a coma and tail only when they are heated by the Sun’s radiation, causing sublimation of their icy components.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is least likely to contribute to the disruption of a comet’s nucleus?

options.text: Sublimation of volatiles

options.text: Tidal forces from the Sun or Jupiter
options.explanation: Tidal forces are a well-documented process that can disrupt a comet’s nucleus.

options.text: Collisions with other comets
